questions.question: Discuss the grading, packing, and storage practices for gerbera cut flowers. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the grading, packing, and storage practices for gerbera cut flowers. [K / CO2]
  • • Grading: Based on stalk length, stalk thickness and strength, flower diameter, freedom
  • from pests, diseases, mechanical damage, flower form, and colour.
  • • Packing: Flower stalks are soaked in solutions such as sodium hypochlorite; flowers are
  • sorted into uniform lots, aligned, and bundled. Packaging should prevent bending,
  • crushing, moisture loss, and mechanical injury.
  • • Storage: Pre -cooled soon after harvest, stored at low temperature and high relative
  • humidity. Clean water or holding solutions maintain hydration. (Any 5 valuable points - 5
  • marks)

questions.question: Explain the spatial zoning of a kitchen garden. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the spatial zoning of a kitchen garden. [K / CO1]
  • • Zone 1 (Immediate Kitchen Access): Reserve the area within 5 –10 steps of the kitchen
  • door for high-frequency harvest items—Curry Leaf, Kanthari chili, Panikoorkka, Mint, and
  • coriander/microgreens.
  • • Zone 2 (Sunlit Garden Beds): Position raised beds or grow bags in spots receiving 6+ hours
  • of sunlight for sun-loving seasonal vegetables like tomatoes, okra (Vendakka), and gourds.
  • • Zone 3 (Perimeter & Canopy): Place tall fruit trees and coconut palms along property
  • boundaries to serve as windbreaks and privacy screens without overshadowing the core
  • vegetable zones.

questions.question: Describe the concept of training in crop plants. Discuss its objectives and various methods with suitable examples. / [CO2] [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the concept of training in crop plants. Discuss its objectives and various
  • methods with suitable examples. [K / CO2]
  • Definition: Training is the practice of directing and controlling the growth of a young fruit
  • plant into a desired shape or framework by tying, supporting, bending, or selectively removing
  • shoots. (2 marks)
  • Objectives of Training: (Any 2 points - 2 marks)
  • - Develop a strong framework capable of bearing heavy fruit loads.
  • - Maintain proper tree shape and size.
  • - Improve light penetration and air circulation.
  • - Facilitate orchard operations (pruning, spraying, harvesting, intercultural operations).
  • - Increase photosynthetic efficiency and reduce wind/load breakage.
  • - Improve fruit colour, size, quality, and pest management.
  • Methods of Training: (Any 4 methods with examples - 6 marks)
  • Open Centre System (Vase System): Central leader removed after planting; 3-5 scaffold branches
  • grow outward forming an open centre for better sunlight. Eg: Apple, peach, mango, guava.
  • Central Leader System: Main trunk grows uninterrupted; lateral branches arise regularly, forming a
  • pyramidal shape with strong structural support. Eg: Pear, walnut, sapota.
  • Cordon System: Single strong shoot grown to desired height, then bent and tied horizontally along
  • supporting wires to form permanent arms maintained by annual pruning. Eg: Grapes, passion
  • fruit, vanilla.
  • Head System (Bush System): Main trunk kept short (30-90 cm). 4-6 primary branches arise from
  • the head giving a bush-like appearance. Eg: Grapes, pepper.
  • Bower (Pergola) System: Vines grow over an overhead network of wires supported by pillars to
  • form a roof-like canopy. Eg: Grapes, passion fruit, bitter gourd.
  • [10 x 1 = 10 Marks]
